How Kafka consumer groups share partitions

Posted on 14 September 2025 by Priya N.

A consumer group is a set of consumers that cooperate to read a topic. Kafka assigns each partition of the topic to exactly one consumer in the group, so the work is split without two consumers ever reading the same message.

When a consumer joins or leaves, the group rebalances: the group coordinator takes the partitions back and hands them out again. During a rebalance nobody in the group makes progress, which is why long rebalances show up as consumer lag.

Offsets record progress

Each consumer commits an offset per partition. The offset says how far the group has read, so after a rebalance the new owner of a partition can carry on from the last committed position instead of starting again.

  • Commit after processing to get at-least-once delivery.
  • Commit before processing to get at-most-once delivery.

More consumers than partitions

A group can never have more active consumers than the topic has partitions. Extra consumers sit idle, waiting for a partition to free up. If you need more parallelism, add partitions first.

Partitions are the unit of parallelism in Kafka.

That is the whole trick: partitions bound parallelism, offsets bound replay, and the coordinator keeps the two in step.
